questions.q: A statistically insignificant α with positive sign most likely means:
o: Noise — do not over-fund the strategy; check t-stat, sample length, and style drift
questions.why: Positive α without significance: cannot reject luck — sizing and mandate changes must rest on the confidence interval, not the point estimate.

questions.q: If a security plots BELOW the SML, it is:
o: Overvalued — its required return is higher than CAPM-implied for its beta? — no: below SML gives lower return than required ⇒ overpriced; sell/avoid
questions.why: Below SML: expected return < required return ⇒ price too high — sell. Above: buy. Many 'below ⇒ cheap' options are the trap.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the above/below direction question is the SML's only real test Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: The line is fairness: below it you're overpriced, above it underpriced.

questions.q: The Capital Market Line plots expected return against:
questions.why: CML = efficient portfolios only, y-axis vs TOTAL risk (σ); SML uses systematic risk (β) for any asset.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the axes-of-the-lines distinction is definition-perfect AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: CML grades the finished portfolio by σ; SML grades every asset by β.

questions.q: For evaluating a fully diversified equity portfolio against the market, the appropriate single-number ratio is:
questions.why: Treynor and α suit well-diversified portfolios (systematic risk basis); Sharpe suits total-risk/standalone funds. ICAI expects picking by risk-appropriateness.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — ratio-selection by risk basis AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Total soup → Sharpe; pure market exposure → Treynor; manager skill → α.

questions.q: For a mutual-fund manager benchmarking relative to a market index with the SAME risk, the right measure of excess return per unit systematic risk is:
questions.why: Treynor = (Rp − Rf)/βp — excess per unit beta; Sharpe uses total risk; IR uses tracking-error denominator for active risk.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
